# czc-v2026.10.27.1 (0.2.18.3)

Stops stalled Grok turns from hanging for up to 58 minutes. A Grok upstream
that keeps sending keepalive data after the model has stopped producing output
is now detected within the configured idle window and failed over (before
output) or closed with a normal terminal chunk (after output).

## Changes since czc-v2026.10.26.3

- Grok stream idle is now measured against model progress instead of raw
  bytes. Vendor `event: ping` frames, SSE comments, blank lines,
  `response.queued` / `response.in_progress`, repeated `response.created` and
  empty deltas no longer reset the idle timer. Previously any of these kept a
  stalled turn alive until the 58m wall-clock abort while clients showed an
  endless "thinking" state. Production showed 11 such xhigh turns in the 7
  days before this release, on both `cli-chat-proxy.grok.com` and
  `api.x.ai` accounts.
- Applies to both the Grok Chat Completions bridge
  (`gateway.grok_stream_data_interval_timeout`, default 600s for xhigh and
  180s otherwise) and Grok Responses streams
  (`gateway.stream_data_interval_timeout`). Non-Grok platforms keep the
  existing byte-level idle behavior.
- The Grok idle deadline is checked every `min(idle/4, 15s)` instead of once
  per idle interval, which could detect a stall only after up to twice the
  interval.
- After the client disconnects, a Grok upstream that makes no progress for
  120s is closed instead of being drained until the wall clock. Upstreams that
  are still producing output continue to be drained so usage remains billable.
- Each Grok idle timeout writes a Warn log and an ops upstream-error event
  with diagnostic counters (time since last progress and last read, last
  event type, lines, comments, pings, idle and progress events).
- The idle message is now `Grok stream idle timeout after <n> with no
  upstream progress`.

## VERSION

`0.2.18.3`

## Upgrade guidance and compatibility

- No database migration, frontend source change or configuration change is
  required. Defaults are unchanged; only the meaning of the Grok idle timeout
  changes from "no bytes" to "no model progress".
- In the 7 days before this release the longest Grok time to first visible
  output was 190s, below the 600s xhigh and 180s default windows. Operators
  who run Grok models with longer silent reasoning can raise
  `gateway.grok_stream_data_interval_timeout` (30–1800s).
- Restarting the service closes existing streams; clients should resend
  interrupted turns.

## Verification

Passed on the implementation/integration tree before packaging:

- Full backend unit suite on `dev-czc` after merging the fix:
  `go test -count=1 -tags=unit ./...` (exit 0).
- golangci-lint v2.14.0 `run ./...` on the same tree: 0 issues.
- `go vet` (with and without the `unit` tag) for `internal/service` and
  `internal/config`, `gofmt -l` clean, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`.
- 13 new unit tests covering progress classification, check interval,
  disconnected drain cap, ping-only, comment-only and repeated
  `response.in_progress` upstreams, steady progress outliving the idle window
  on both the Chat Completions bridge and the Responses path, disconnected
  drain, and unchanged non-Grok keepalive behavior.
- Regression proof: with the fix's two stream handlers reverted, the
  ping-only, comment keepalive, repeated in_progress and disconnected-drain
  tests hung until the 2-minute test timeout, reproducing the production
  stall. With the fix restored they pass in 1-2s each.
- Read-only production review: 7-day Grok time to first visible output is at
  most 190s (none above 300s); 11 xhigh turns stalled for 20-58 minutes after
  a few hundred output tokens, matching the fixed failure mode.

Failed, interrupted or not performed:

- The first full unit-suite and two golangci-lint runs were killed by tool
  time limits before finishing and were not counted; both were rerun to
  completion with the results above.
- Docker-backed integration tests (`-tags=integration`), backend e2e and
  browser end-to-end tests were not run. The change is limited to Grok stream
  handling in `internal/service` and is covered by unit tests.
- Frontend lint/type/Vitest checks were not run; there is no frontend source
  change. The frontend is still rebuilt before the embed build.
- No live Grok upstream stall was reproduced against production accounts; the
  stall is simulated with scripted SSE bodies.

Packaging must rebuild the frontend immediately before the `-tags embed`
server build from this exact tag, with `main.ReleaseURL` set to this origin
release. Installation is accepted only after the root page returns HTTP 200,
the installed version is `0.2.18.3`, and the running update-check response
reports this same release URL.

## Rollback

Restore the binary backed up during this deploy as
`/opt/sub2api/sub2api.bak.czc-v2026.10.27.1-<UTC timestamp>` and restart
`sub2api.service`, or rebuild and deploy `czc-v2026.10.26.3` (`0.2.18.2`).
There is no database migration or configuration change to undo. Verify HTTP
200, version `0.2.18.2` and the previous origin release URL after rollback.
